candidates.title: Pembrolizumab-Associated Adrenal Insufficiency Presenting as Adrenal Crisis: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Immunotherapy regimens containing the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor pembrolizumab are widely utilised in the management of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the administration of pembrolizumab is associated with unique immune-related adverse events. Adrenal insufficiency is a rare, potentially life-threatening endocrinopathy that can manifest even after the cessation of planned treatment. A male in his 50s with metastatic pulmonary adenocarcinoma developed an acute adrenal crisis 12 days after completing a 24-month course of pembrolizumab immunotherapy. Routine outpatient blood tests first identified critical hypocortisolaemia (morning serum cortisol <50 nmol/L), prompting the patient to attend hospital. The patient subsequently developed severe hypotension (58/45 mmHg) and reported malaise, anorexia, and vomiting after oral intake. Septic shock was considered but felt to be less likely given the absence of infective symptoms. The patient was successfully resuscitated in the emergency department with administration of fluids and high-dose intravenous hydrocortisone. Following clinical stabilisation, under the supervision of the endocrinology team, he was transitioned to a long-term oral maintenance regimen consisting of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. This case illustrates that pembrolizumab-associated adrenal insufficiency can present as an abrupt, life-threatening crisis in the immediate post-treatment phase. Frontline clinicians must remain vigilant for late-onset endocrinopathies, regardless of the treatment completion date. Proactive patient education and long-term biochemical surveillance are imperative to ensuring early clinical intervention and avoiding catastrophic management delays and poor clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Acinetobacter baumannii Nosocomial Meningitis Secondary to Neurosurgical Intervention: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Nosocomial meningitis is a serious complication of neurosurgical procedures, associated with high morbidity and mortality, as well as significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Among the causative pathogens, Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) is particularly concerning due to its ability to survive for prolonged periods in the hospital environment, its opportunistic virulence, and, especially, its tendency to develop multidrug resistance to antimicrobial agents. Diagnosis is often difficult in the postoperative setting, particularly when the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is altered as a result of the surgical procedure. Rapid identification of the causative agent and early initiation of appropriate antibiotic therapy are essential to limit complications and improve patient prognosis. We report the case of a 27-year-old patient with a history of surgically treated craniopharyngioma complicated by anterior hypopituitarism. Three weeks after surgery, he was admitted to the ICU with suspected postoperative meningitis due to the onset of behavioral disturbances associated with nasal discharge, without a fever. Brain CT was normal. CSF analysis, obtained by lumbar puncture under strict aseptic conditions, revealed a turbid fluid with leukocytosis of 5,760 cells/mm³, predominantly composed of neutrophils, along with elevated protein levels (5.7 g/L) and low glucose levels (0.05 g/L). Direct examination after Gram staining showed Gram-negative coccobacilli with a marked inflammatory reaction. CSF culture grew a multidrug-resistant (MDR) strain of A. baumannii, which was sensitive only to colistin. The patient received antibiotic therapy with colistin, administered intravenously and intrathecally for 18 days, with initial neurological improvement and sterilization of the CSF by the 15th day of treatment. The subsequent course was unfavorable, marked by the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), complicated by refractory septic shock, which ultimately led to his death after one month of hospitalization in the ICU. This report highlights the severity of nosocomial meningitis caused by MDR A. baumannii and underscores the importance of implementing infection prevention measures in healthcare settings.

candidates.title: Medullary thyroid carcinoma with pheochromocytoma and cystic parathyroid degeneration in a ret-negative patient: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN2A) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary cancer syndrome, predominantly caused by mutations of the RET proto-oncogene on chromosome 10q11.2. It typically presents with medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism. Cases with a MEN2A phenotype but negative RET testing are uncommon, posing challenges for diagnosis and patient management. We report the case of a 63-year-old female who was diagnosed with MTC and pheochromocytoma. and cystic parathyroid gland. Genetic workup was negative for RET proto-oncogene mutations but positive for a heterozygous variant in the TMEM127 tumor suppressor gene. MEN2A is associated with pathogenic germline variants in the RET proto-oncogene in approximately 95-99% of cases. Our patient, however, exhibited a MEN2A-like clinical phenotype in the absence of an identifiable RET mutation, with a pathogenic TMEM127 variant instead. Although TMEM127 is an established susceptibility gene for pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, its association with the broader MEN2A phenotype remains unclear. This unusual genotype-phenotype discordance raises important questions regarding the potential role of alternative genetic pathways in MEN2-like syndromes and creates uncertainty regarding postoperative surveillance and the appropriate extent of screening and genetic counseling for family members. Our case represents an unusual scenario where the patient presents with a clinical phenotype of MEN2A but is RET negative and positive heterozygous for a variant in the TMEM127. This atypical genetic finding introduces complexities in determining the appropriate follow-up protocol and the scope of familial screening necessary.

candidates.title: Prevalence and spectrum of variants in homologous recombination repair genes in ovarian cancer in Latin America: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract: Ovarian cancer is a major cause of gynecologic cancer mortality worldwide, with disproportionately poor outcomes in Latin America (LATAM). Variants in homologous recombination repair genes, especially BRCA1/2, are predictive biomarkers for platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors. However, data on the prevalence and spectrum of homologous recombination repair variants in LATAM populations remain limited. To synthesize the prevalence and spectrum of pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants in homologous recombination repair pathway genes among LATAM ovarian cancer patients and highlight clinical and research implications. The review protocol was developed in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and was registered in the international prospective register of systematic reviews (PROSPERO; registration number CRD420251019706). We systematically searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, LILACS, Cochrane, and Epistemonikos through April 2025. Eligible studies included LATAM ovarian cancer patients tested with multigene panels covering homologous recombination repair genes beyond BRCA1/2. Data extraction followed 2025 ACMG/AMP guidelines, and study quality was assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Pooled prevalence was estimated using random- and common-effects meta-analysis. Eight studies published between 2017 and 2023, including 442 patients with ovarian cancer from Brazil, Argentina, Mexico, Chile, and Colombia, were included in the systematic review. Following variant curation and reclassification, 7 studies comprising 433 patients and 96 pathogenic/likely pathogenic homologous recombination repair variant carriers were retained for prevalence analysis, yielding a crude prevalence of 22.2%. Pathogenic variants predominated (91.7%), with BRCA1 (55.2%) and BRCA2 (40.6%) accounting for ∼96% of carriers. Non-BRCA homologous recombination repair variants (CHEK2, BARD1, and RAD51D) accounted for 4.2%. The pooled prevalence of germline pathogenic/likely pathogenic homologous recombination repair variants was 17% (95% CI, 9%-26%; I²=56.2%), increasing to 20% (95% CI, 16%-23%; I²=0%) after sensitivity analysis excluding 2 micro-cohorts. Five recurrent variants were identified across multiple cohorts and countries. No study evaluated somatic homologous recombination repair variants or homologous recombination deficiency assays. This first systematic synthesis of homologous recombination repair variants in LATAM ovarian cancer reveals a predominance of BRCA1/2 but also underscores the relevance of non-BRCA homologous recombination repair genes. Lack of somatic testing, methodological heterogeneity, and limited regional coverage highlight the need for standardized approaches, multicenter collaboration, and equitable access to genomic diagnostics in the region. This systematic review highlights both opportunities and barriers for implementing homologous recombination repair testing in ovarian cancer across Latin America. While BRCA1/2 remains the predominant genes, non-BRCA variants are also clinically relevant. Importantly, we identified substantial inequities in the distribution of genomic testing capacity, with most data concentrated in Brazil and Argentina, leaving many countries unrepresented. The absence of somatic homologous recombination repair/homologous recombination deficiency testing and heterogeneous sequencing approaches further limit regional comparability and access to precision therapies. Addressing these disparities through standardized testing strategies and collaborative networks is critical to ensure equitable access to genetic counseling and targeted treatments.

candidates.title: Pembrolizumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin for advanced biliary tract cancer: longer-term follow-up from the randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 KEYNOTE-966 trial.
candidates.abstract: At the final analysis of KEYNOTE-966 (median follow-up 25·6 months), pembrolizumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (pembrolizumab group) versus placebo plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (placebo group) provided a statistically significant, clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival without any new safety signals in participants with advanced biliary tract cancer. We report results from a median study follow-up of 36·6 months (∼3 years). In the randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 KEYNOTE-966 trial conducted at 175 medical centres worldwide, eligible participants aged ≥18 years with previously untreated advanced biliary tract cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) to pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo intravenously every 3 weeks plus gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and cisplatin 25 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1 and 8 of every 3-week cycle. Randomisation was done using a central interactive voice-response system and stratified by geographical region, disease status, and site of origin in block sizes of four. The primary endpoint of overall survival was evaluated in the intention-to-treat population (all participants randomly assigned to a treatment). Safety was evaluated in the as-treated population, comprising all participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. As the primary endpoint was met at the final analysis, updated data are reported without p values. This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04003636. Between Oct 4, 2019, and June 8, 2021, 1069 participants were randomly assigned to the pembrolizumab group (n = 533) or the placebo group (n = 536). Median follow-up at data cutoff (Nov 14, 2023) was 36·6 months (IQR 32·7-41·4). The hazard ratio for overall survival was 0·86 (95% CI, 0·75-0·98) with pembrolizumab versus placebo; estimated 36-month overall survival rates were 13% (95% CI, 11-17) in the pembrolizumab group and 11% (95% CI, 8-14) in the placebo group. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 370 (70%) of 529 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 367 (69%) of 534 participants in the placebo group. No new treatment-related deaths occurred since the final analysis. With extended follow-up, the survival benefit of pembrolizumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin observed at the final analysis persists with approximately 3 years of follow-up, with no new safety signals among participants with previously untreated metastatic or unresectable biliary tract cancer. candidates.title: Endocrine therapies and hormonal dysfunction after traumatic brain injury: A scoping review.
candidates.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with current management strategies primarily focused on preventing secondary injury rather than modifying disease progression. Post-traumatic endocrine dysfunction has emerged as a significant and potentially treatable contributor to outcomes after TBI. A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 2025 for clinical studies evaluating endocrine dysfunction and endocrine-targeted therapies post-TBI. Eligible studies included clinical trials and observational studies reporting either an endocrine outcome following TBI or an endocrine-targeted intervention with clinical or biochemical outcomes. Sixty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Endocrine dysfunction was common, affecting multiple hormone axes, with growth hormone (GH) deficiency being the most frequently reported deficiency; hypoprolactinemia and hyperprolactinemia were also identified and are increasingly recognized contributors to post-TBI metabolic morbidity. Growth hormone replacement therapy demonstrated improvements in cognitive function, fatigue, mood, and quality of life in several studies; however, its effects on functional outcomes and mortality were inconsistent. Progesterone showed benefit in early-phase trials but failed to demonstrate efficacy in large multicenter randomized controlled trials, an inconsistency that appears closely tied to the timing of treatment initiation after injury. Other therapies, including desmopressin and glucocorticoids, were primarily used for supportive management, with limited evidence of neuroprotective benefit. Endocrine dysfunction after TBI is prevalent, heterogeneous, and associated with worse clinical outcomes. While endocrine therapies, particularly GH, show promise, their translation into clinical practice is limited by heterogeneity in study design, small sample sizes, and inconsistent findings. Larger, well-designed trials and consensus clinical guidelines are needed to define optimal therapeutic strategies and integrate endocrine care into the optimal management of TBI patients.
candidates.journal: Growth hormone & IGF research : official journal of the Growth Hormone Research Society and the International IGF Research Society

candidates.title: Oncological Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Adjuvant Nivolumab in Muscle-Invasive Urothelial Carcinoma.
candidates.abstract: Perioperative immunotherapy has become the standard of care in patients with high-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma (MIUC). This study aimed to clarify oncological outcomes and safety profiles of adjuvant nivolumab therapy in MIUC, focusing on upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). This multicenter study comprised 97 patients undergoing removal of primary tumors, followed by adjuvant nivolumab therapy with a potential follow-up period ≥ 12 months. Patients were divided according to the primary tumor location: bladder cancer (BC), n = 66 (68%); UTUC, n = 31 (32%). Multivariable Cox regression analyses were applied to identify prognostic factors for disease-free survival (DFS). Before surgery, 38% of patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 50 mL/min/1.73m2, but this proportion increased to 57% at nivolumab initiation with 19% of UTUC having eGFR < 30. The overall DFS at 6 months was 61.5%. DFS did not differ significantly between BC and UTUC (p = 0.83). On multivariable analyses, a higher absolute eosinophil count was significantly associated with worse DFS (HR 2.24; 95% CI, 1.24-4.03, p = 0.007), while primary tumor location was not. Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) of adrenal insufficiency and hypophysitis occurred in 8% and 4% of patients, respectively, with grade ≥ 3 occurring at 3.3-18.3 months. Adjuvant nivolumab therapy may provide comparable oncological outcomes between BC and UTUC. Baseline eosinophil count was an independent prognosticator for DFS. The incidences of adrenal insufficiency and hypophysitis appeared higher in our real-world data. Clinicians should recognize these irAEs due to nonspecific symptoms and considerable variability in time of onset.
candidates.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association

candidates.title: Pediatric sellar and parasellar lesions: a population-based cohort study of presentation, management, and endocrine outcomes.
candidates.abstract: Population-based studies describing the full clinical spectrum of pediatric sellar and parasellar lesions are scarce. Most available data derive from referral-based surgical or diagnosis-specific cohorts. We aimed to characterize presentation, lesion pathology, management, and long-term endocrine outcomes in a population-based cohort. We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study of patients aged 18 years or younger diagnosed with sellar or parasellar lesions between 1976 and 2021 in a multicounty region. Clinical presentation, lesion characteristics, management, and endocrine outcomes were abstracted from medical records. Associations were evaluated by lesion type, lesion size (< 10 mm vs. ≥10 mm), and management approach. Among 104 patients, endocrine abnormalities at diagnosis differed by lesion type (p = 0.0004) and were most frequent among patients with pituitary adenomas. Endocrine dysfunction at presentation was more common with lesions ≥ 10 mm than with lesions < 10 mm (74.2% vs. 49.2%; p = 0.0217). Post-treatment endocrine abnormalities were also more common with lesions ≥ 10 mm (64.5% vs. 13.1%; p < 0.0001). Associations with treatment modality were descriptive and subject to confounding by indication. This population-based cohort captured a broad spectrum of pediatric sellar and parasellar disease, including uncommon lesions and conservatively managed cases. Endocrine morbidity was associated with lesion type and size, but clinically relevant abnormalities also occurred in smaller lesions, supporting endocrine evaluation based on clinical context and longitudinal surveillance.

candidates.title: The Effect of Digital Storytelling on the Anxiety of Patients with Pituitary Adenoma Undergoing Transsphenoidal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract: Patients with pituitary adenoma often experience anxiety due to hormonal changes and the stress associated with transsphenoidal surgery. Digital storytelling, as an innovative multimedia-based training method, has recently been used in patient education. This study investigated the effect of digital storytelling on the anxiety of patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery. This randomized controlled trial was conducted on 70 patients with pituitary adenoma scheduled for transsphenoidal surgery at a teaching hospital affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention or a control group. The intervention group received a 15-20-minute digital storytelling program that included experiences shared by patients and nurses regarding preoperative and postoperative care, while the control group received routine hospital education. Anxiety levels were measured a day before surgery, a day after surgery, and three weeks later using Spielberger's State Anxiety Scale. Data were analyzed by SPSS-25 software using descriptive and inferential statistics. The mean score of anxiety in the intervention group decreased by 12.45 (1.24) units a day after the surgery and by 24.82 (1.32) units three weeks after the surgery compared to baseline (p < 0.001). A significantly lower anxiety level was observed in the intervention group at both post-intervention time periods compared to the pre-intervention time (F = 17.05, p < 0.001). Repeated measures Analysis of Variance confirmed a significant interaction between time and group (F = 25.31, p < 0.001). Digital storytelling was effective in reducing anxiety among patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery and may serve as a valuable educational intervention.
candidates.journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research

candidates.title: A Clinical Insight into Von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome: Diagnostic Challenges.
candidates.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome is a rare hereditary disorder characterised by the development of multiple benign and malignant tumours across various organs. Caused by mutations in the VHL tumour suppressor gene, it presents a wide range of clinical manifestations, including retinal haemangioblastomas, central nervous system tumours, renal cell carcinoma, pancreatic lesions, and phaeochromocytomas. This report describes the case of a 35-year-old woman who presented with visual impairment and abdominal masses. Imaging revealed typical VHL manifestations, including bilateral renal lesions and pancreatic involvement. Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis. The patient underwent staged partial nephrectomies, with histopathology confirming clear cell renal cell carcinoma in both kidneys. This case highlights the importance of recognising the variable clinical and radiological presentations of VHL syndrome. Early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management are essential to reduce morbidity and mortality. Increased awareness and regular surveillance are critical for timely detection and intervention in patients with VHL syndrome.

candidates.title: Psychopathological and psychosexual profile and therapy for patients with androgen insensitivity syndrome: a narrative review.
candidates.abstract: The objective of this review is to present androgen insensitivity syndrome as a multidimensional disorder, with a focus on psychological issues, gender identity, and sexual functioning. It also discusses therapeutic options, such as psychological and psychiatric support. Androgen insensitivity syndrome is a rare disorder of sex development that occurs in individuals with an XY karyotype. It is caused by a mutation in the androgen receptor gene, leading to reduced sensitivity to androgens. There are three forms: mild, partial, and complete androgen insensitivity syndrome. Individuals with a 46,XY karyotype may exhibit female, male, or ambiguous phy-sical characteristics. This condition is associated with medical, psychological, sexual, and gender identity difficulties. Those affected may experience depression, anxiety, and suicidal thoughts. Those with complete androgen insensitivity syndrome usually identify as female, while those with partial androgen insensitivity syndrome often experience gender identity conflicts and sexual dysfunction. Patients with androgen insensitivity syndrome experience issues with sexuality, gender identity, and mental health. Every patient needs a personalized approach that includes medical and psychological support. The diagnosis and treatment of androgen insensitivity syndrome should not only consider medical interventions. A long-term care model is necessary that considers spheres of life such as identity, sexuality, and mental health. A comprehensive approach can improve quality of life and minimize the risk of future psychological and psychosexual problems.

candidates.title: Nutritional and physiological response to feed form and sodium bicarbonate-adjusted dietary electrolyte balance in lactating sows under heat stress.
candidates.abstract: Heat stress (HS) during lactation poses a critical challenge in swine production, often impairing feed intake, metabolic function, and reproductive performance in sows. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of feed form (mash vs. pellet) and dietary electrolyte balance (dEB; 230 vs. 290 mEq/kg) adjusted with sodium bicarbonate on sow performance, litter growth, immune response, antioxidant status, and gut microbiota under HS conditions. A total of 40 multiparous sows were assigned to four treatments in a 2 × 2 factorial design: Mlow (mash + 230 mEq/kg), Mhigh (mash + 290 mEq/kg), Plow (pellet + 230 mEq/kg), and Phigh (pellet + 290 mEq/kg). Each treatment contained 10 sows with 3-5 parity and their initial body weight was 241.83 ± 16 kg at d 112 of lactation. The trial spanned from parturition to weaning (21 days) during summer at an average temperature of 28.8°C. Results showed that sows fed pelleted diets (Plow, Phigh) and higher dEB levels (Mhigh, Phigh) had higher (p < 0.001) average daily feed intake. Piglets from Mhigh and Phigh sows had increased (p = 0.001) weaning weights. Dry matter digestibility was increased (p = 0.022) in sows receiving pelleted diets. The tumour necrosis factor-alpha was lower (p < 0.001) in Plow, Phigh, and Mhigh (p = 0.010), with an interaction (p = 0.013) in feed forms and dEB. The interleukin-1β was lower (p < 0.001) in Plow and Phigh, with higher (p < 0.001) superoxide dismutase activity in Phigh and Plow. Hair cortisol was lower (p = 0.048) in pelleted groups, suggesting lower physiological stress. Although alpha diversity did not differ, beta diversity and relative abundance of Lactobacillus and Turicibacter indicated microbial shifts influenced by feed form. In conclusion, pelleted feed form and higher dEB, particularly the Phigh treatment, enhanced feed intake, litter performance, and anti-inflammatory status without negatively affecting milk composition or gut integrity. These findings support the integration of feed form and electrolyte strategies to improve sow productivity under HS conditions.
candidates.journal: Journal of animal science and technology

candidates.title: Sinonasal and Olfactory Quality of Life Following Endonasal Transsphenoidal Surgery for Pituitary Adenoma: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Triphasic Recovery Analysis in Ethiopia.
candidates.abstract: To characterize the sinonasal and olfactory quality of life (QoL) trajectory. A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted on 91 patients undergoing TSS at Addis Ababa University teaching hospitals between May 2024 and August 2025. QoL was evaluated using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) questionnaire v4 preoperatively and at 3- and 6-month postoperatively. Analysis revealed a characteristic triphasic recovery pattern: low preoperative baseline, a transient peak in morbidity at 3 months, and an improvement toward baseline by 6 months for most systemic domains. At 3 months, significant score worsening occurred for loss of smell/taste (mean: 1.7, p < 0.001), thick discharge (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), congestion (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), postnasal discharge (mean: 0.7, p < 0.001), and runny nose (mean: 0.5, p = 0.003). By 6 months, persistence was confined to loss of smell/taste (p < 0.001), thick discharge (p < 0.001), and congestion (p = 0.005). Exploratory analysis in the nasoseptal flap cohort (n = 3) showed higher scores. Preliminary findings of delayed ear pain/fullness in acromegaly at 6 months hypothesized to reflect a link between growth hormone normalization and altered Eustachian tube function. Poorer sleep with binostril access (p = 0.017) speculatively associated with bilateral synechiae under limited postoperative care. Unlike Western cohorts, protracted recovery may reflect lack of standardized high-volume saline irrigation and scheduled debridement. TSS demonstrates a favorable long-term QoL profile; however, localized sinonasal and olfactory deficits often persist at 6 months.

candidates.title: Structured Physiotherapy Improves Functional Outcomes in Acromegalic Arthropathy After Biochemical Remission: A Prospective Controlled Study.
candidates.abstract: Musculoskeletal symptoms frequently persist in acromegaly despite biochemical remission, yet the impact of structured physiotherapy on pain, stiffness, and function remains poorly defined. To evaluate the effects of a standardized knee-focused physiotherapy program in controlled acromegaly and to identify clinical predictors of treatment responsiveness. Thirteen patients with acromegaly in remission and 13 age-, gender-, and BMI-matched individuals with primary knee osteoarthritis completed a 15-session physiotherapy program. Outcomes were assessed pre- and post-intervention using the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI) and WOMAC. Minimal clinically significant difference (MCID) thresholds (≥2 for BPI, ≥10 for WOMAC) determined meaningful improvement. Correlation analyses examined associations between clinical variables and Δ scores. Acromegaly patients showed significant improvements in all BPI and WOMAC domains (p<0.001). MCID was achieved by 85% for BPI and 100% for WOMAC Total. Pain and function improved most, whereas stiffness showed limited responsiveness. Compared with osteoarthritis controls, acromegaly patients demonstrated smaller Δ changes; baseline-adjusted analyses (ANCOVA) indicated that this attenuated response was largely explained by greater baseline severity in the control group, whereas the persistently greater stiffness in acromegaly remained significant even after adjustment. BMI correlated positively with improvements in BPI Total (r = 0.63) and BPI Pain Severity (r = 0.69), while adenoma size correlated negatively with both measures (r = -0.57 and -0.60). BMI showed a negative association with WOMAC Total improvement (r = -0.59). Stiffness changes were strongly negatively correlated with pretreatment IGF-1 (r = -0.77). Structured physiotherapy yields clinically meaningful improvements in pain and function in acromegaly, while stiffness appears less reversible and more structurally driven. Early musculoskeletal assessment and physiotherapy integration may enhance long-term management.

candidates.title: Microbiological aetiology of paediatric ventilator-associated pneumonia and risk factors for carbapenem-resistant acinetobacter and Pseudomonas in a tertiary-care hospital in Thailand.
candidates.abstract: Paediatric ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) worsens outcomes and mortality. Characterizing local microbiology and resistance patterns is crucial for empirical therapy and guiding targeted infection prevention and control. This study aimed to determine the aetiology of VAP, identify risk factors associated with VAP caused by carbapenem-resistant (CR) Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas, and assess the clinical burden and outcomes of VAP in paediatric patients. We conducted a retrospective study of patients under 18 years of age diagnosed with VAP between January 2022 and December 2024, using Centres for Disease Control and Prevention/National Healthcare Safety Network (CDC/NHSN) surveillance criteria. Data including demographics, microbiology, and outcomes were retrieved from electronic medical records. Risk factors for CR-VAP were assessed using logistic regression. A total of 71 VAP patients with 95 episodes, were analysed (median age: 7.1 months [interquartile range {IQR}, 2-63]; 49% male). The VAP incidence rate showed a decreasing trend (9.1 to 4.7 per 1000 ventilator-days, 2022-2024). The median time to VAP onset was 25 days (IQR, 13-51) postintubation. The predominant isolated pathogens were Gram-negative bacteria, specifically Acinetobacter baumannii (22%; 64% CR), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (19%; 56% CR), and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (19%). Staphylococcus aureus (8%; 21% Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus [MRSA]) was the most common Gram-positive isolate. Thirteen patients (18%) experienced multiple VAP episodes. The overall 90-day mortality rate was 24%. Prolonged hospitalization was linked to carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB) (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.3; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.36-13.61; P = 0.013), while prolonged intubation was associated with carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa (CRPA) (aOR, 6.61; 95% CI, 1.42-30.85; P = 0.016). VAP remains a challenge in the paediatric setting, characterized by a high prevalence of multi-drug-resistant pathogens, particularly CR Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas. Continued surveillance, antimicrobial stewardship, and intensified prevention are essential to reduce VAP burden and improve outcomes.

candidates.title: A Case of MEN 2A Syndrome With Bilateral Recurrent Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from chromaffin cells and producing catecholamines. Due to the excessive release of catecholamines, these tumors can present with paroxysmal episodes of high blood pressure, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient who presented to the clinic with a history of headache, palpitations, and vomiting for two months. She was admitted for further investigations and management. Laboratory studies revealed elevated urinary and plasma catecholamine levels. Further work-up revealed bilateral adrenal masses diagnosed as pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer. The patient was diagnosed with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 2 and underwent bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy and total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection, and during surveillance, she was found to have recurrent pheochromocytoma. We also discuss the diagnosis and management of recurrent pheochromocytoma in MEN syndrome.

candidates.title: From Trauma to Tumour: Incidental Giant Left Adrenal Myelolipoma in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal myelolipomas are rare, benign tumours composed of mature adipose and haematopoietic tissue. Patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) are predisposed to their development, with chronic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) hypersecretion secondary to impaired cortisol synthesis thought to be the principal driver of myelolipoma formation in this population. A 49-year-old female with known CAH presented to the emergency department following a stab wound to the abdomen. Computed tomography (CT) incidentally identified a 12 cm encapsulated left adrenal lesion consistent with a giant myelolipoma. Despite reported adherence to hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone replacement therapy, persistently elevated adrenal steroid precursors and plasma renin levels suggested suboptimal glucocorticoid control. Following multidisciplinary team (MDT) review, the patient was offered a left adrenalectomy given the lesion size (>10 cm) and concerns regarding the risk of spontaneous haemorrhage. This case underscores the importance of systematic imaging review beyond the primary indication for scanning, and the value of optimising biochemical monitoring and considering adrenal imaging in selected high-risk CAH patients.

candidates.title: When Appearances Deceive: A Silent Somatotroph Macroadenoma Presenting With Acromegaloid Features and Paradoxically Low Insulin-Like Growth Factor-1.
candidates.abstract: Silent somatotroph adenomas are uncommon pituitary neuroendocrine tumours (PitNETs) of the PIT1 lineage that express growth hormone (GH) immunohistochemically but without biochemical evidence of acromegaly. We report the case of a 32-year-old male patient referred with recurrent epistaxis, headache, right-sided diplopia, and third cranial nerve palsy. Clinical examination revealed acromegaloid features including frontal bossing, spade-like hands, and coarse facies, which were strongly suggestive of longstanding GH excess. However, preoperative insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) was paradoxically low at 13.1 nmol/L (reference range 15.5-33.1 nmol/L), creating a striking clinical-biochemical discordance. MRI demonstrated a giant sellar and suprasellar mass with chiasmal compression, right cavernous sinus invasion, and extension into the paranasal sinuses. The patient underwent endoscopic transsphenoidal resection. Neuropathology confirmed a densely granulated PIT1-lineage somatotroph adenoma with scattered GH positivity, diffuse Pit-1 staining, and a Ki-67 index below 2%. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by silent somatotroph adenomas, underscores the limitations of biochemical assessment alone, and reinforces the essential role of histopathology and immunohistochemistry in establishing a definitive diagnosis. Long-term endocrine and neurosurgical surveillance is strongly recommended given the potential for phenotypic transformation to a functioning acromegaly syndrome.

candidates.title: Pegvisomant in severe, treatment-resistant thyroid eye disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Teprotumumab, a monoclonal antibody against the IGF1 receptor, has proven effective in the treatment of thyroid eye disease (TED). Pegvisomant reduces IGF1 levels through selective inhibition of growth hormone receptors. Here, we present a hypothesis-generating case of a 69-year-old patient with progressive TED. Pegvisomant 20 mg was administered daily for 90 days. IGF1 levels declined and remained low-normal during treatment. Clinical activity scores and VISA (vision, inflammation, strabismus and appearance) scores improved rapidly. MRI assessment showed that water content of both extraocular muscles and orbital connective tissue decreased after treatment. 99mTc-DTPA SPECT confirmed the decrease in disease activity. Further studies may confirm the efficacy of pegvisomant in TED. A 69-year-old female patient with severe, active thyroid eye disease (TED) – a condition linked to Graves’ disease where the body’s immune system attacks tissues around the eyes – presented with bulging eyes (proptosis), double vision, eye redness, swelling and reduced visual sharpness.Prior treatments with standard therapies for TED, including intravenous steroid courses, radiation therapy targeting the orbit (eye socket) and the biological drug rituximab, failed to achieve improvement. TED progresses in part because proteins called IGF1 receptors on the surface of eye-socket tissues are overactivated. The researchers hypothesized that using pegvisomant, which is a medication typically used for acromegaly (hormone imbalance) that lowers insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) levels in the blood, would reduce activation of these receptors and ease eye inflammation.The patient received a daily 20 mg injection of pegvisomant for 90 days. Symptom improvement The patient experienced a rapid reduction in eye pain, redness and swelling, alongside marked improvement in visual sharpness and colour vision within 8 weeks.MRI and imaging results Orbital MRI and nuclear imaging showed a distinct drop in tissue inflammation and fluid accumulation (oedema) in the muscles around the eye.Proptosis and double vision Eye bulging and double vision did not significantly change during the trial.Safety Pegvisomant was well tolerated with no reported side effects, and her blood sugar and liver function remained stable. Blood IGF1 levels dropped as expected and returned to normal after treatment ended. Pegvisomant rapidly reduced eye inflammation and improved vision in a patient whose TED had resisted standard therapies. However, because this was a single case study, the delayed effects from previous treatments cannot be entirely ruled out. Further clinical trials are needed to determine if pegvisomant is effective at higher doses or when given earlier in the disease course.

candidates.title: Brief Report: Combination Capmatinib and Trametinib in Metastatic MET-Driven NSCLC.
candidates.abstract: MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy has improved outcomes in patients with NSCLC harboring MET alterations. Nevertheless, primary and acquired resistance ultimately limit the durability of response. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of the MET inhibitor capmatinib with the MEK inhibitor trametinib in patients with metastatic MET-driven NSCLC who had progressed on prior treatment with at least one MET inhibitor. A multicenter phase I study evaluated capmatinib in combination with trametinib in patients with advanced-stage NSCLC harboring activating MET alterations and prior exposure to at least one MET TKI. A three-plus-three dose-escalation design was used to assess the safety and tolerability of the combination. Three patients (N = 3) were enrolled in the study and completed a median of three cycles of therapy. Dose-limiting toxicities, including rash, edema, and nausea, necessitated dose reductions in the first two patients and the initiation of therapy in the third patient at a lower dose level. Ultimately, all patients discontinued therapy because of treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). The study was terminated early because of poor accrual and TRAEs. No radiographic objective responses were observed. In this phase I trial, capmatinib plus trametinib was associated with marked TRAEs, and treatment was discontinued in all participants. On the basis of these findings, further investigation of this combination of MET and MEK inhibitors at the tested dose levels is not recommended. Future studies, if pursued, should consider modified dosing strategies, alternative MET and MEK inhibitor combinations, and MET-altered tumors with evidence of MAPK-mediated resistance. NCT05435846.

candidates.title: Genome-scale metabolic modeling-driven design of synbiotics for methane mitigation and quality improvement in fermented total mixed ration.
candidates.abstract: Methane is a major greenhouse gas with a global warming potential 28 times greater than that of carbon dioxide, making reduction of livestock emissions a critical challenge. Current mitigation strategies, such as feed management, chemical additives, and algae supplementation, face limitations related to safety, supply instability, and economic feasibility. To address these issues, we investigated the development of methane-reducing feeds utilizing synbiotics. In a preliminary study, we evaluated the methane reduction potential of Komagataeibacter intermedius and Zygosaccharomyces parabailii (KZ), two SCOBY-derived strains, and identified prebiotics that promote their colonization. Genome-scale metabolic (GSM) models were constructed for three hydrogen-producing bacteria, five methanogens, and the KZ strain, and their metabolic networks were compared. Five prebiotics (glycerol, oleic acid, menaquinone-7, Gly-Leu, and Gly-Asn-L) were identified as substrates utilized by KZ but not by hydrogen-producing bacteria or methanogens. Coculture experiments confirmed that combined prebiotic treatment significantly enhanced KZ growth. In vitro rumen fermentation assays demonstrated reduced methane emissions in synbiotic-treated groups, with the combined prebiotic treatment resulting in the strongest inhibition. Based on these findings, a synbiotic-based fermented total mixed ration (FTMR) was developed. Synbiotic supplementation alleviated acidification, increased acetic acid production, and enriched bacterial and fungal populations. Microbial community analysis revealed higher abundance of lactic acid bacteria and non-Saccharomyces yeasts, indicating improved fermentation and enhanced feed quality. In conclusion, the synbiotic-based FTMR stabilized pH, altered organic acid profiles, and reshaped microbial communities, with synergistic interactions between lactic acid bacteria and yeast supporting a more stable fermentation environment. These results demonstrate that GSM modeling is effective for designing synbiotic-based feeds and that the newly developed synbiotic FTMR improves fermentation quality. Notably, this study focused on prebiotic identification, synbiotic formulation, are fermentation characterization; direct evaluation of the methane reduction efficacy of FTMR under in vitro and in vivo conditions remains a subject for future investigation.
candidates.journal: Journal of animal science and technology

candidates.title: Hair cortisol as a complementary marker of chronic glucocorticoid exposure in mild autonomous cortisol secretion.
candidates.abstract: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion is a subtle yet clinically relevant form of cortisol excess linked to increased cardiometabolic risk. Conventional biochemical tests capture short-term hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity and may not reflect cumulative exposure. Hair cortisol concentration has been proposed as a long-term biomarker, but evidence in mild autonomous cortisol secretion is limited. To compare hair cortisol concentration between patients with mild autonomous cortisol secretion and healthy controls, assess diagnostic performance, and examine associations with hormonal and metabolic parameters. In this cross-sectional study, 73 patients with mild autonomous cortisol secretion and 60 rigorously screened controls were included. Mild autonomous cortisol secretion was defined according to European Society of Endocrinology guidelines. Hair cortisol concentration was measured from the proximal 3-cm hair segment. Assessments included the 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test, 2-day 2 mg dexamethasone suppression test, 24-hour urinary free cortisol, and late-night salivary cortisol. Correlation and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed. Hair cortisol concentration was significantly higher in patients with mild autonomous cortisol secretion than in controls (median 3.6 vs. 1.75 ng/g; p < 0.01). In patients with mild autonomous cortisol secretion, hair cortisol concentration correlated with waist circumference (ρ = 0.27; p = 0.02) and late-night salivary cortisol (ρ = 0.25; p = 0.03), but not with dexamethasone suppression test-based measures or urinary cortisol. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed modest discrimination (AUC = 0.60, 95% CI 0.51-0.70, p = 0.025); the 2.7-ng/g cut-off yielded limited sensitivity and specificity. In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index, hair cortisol concentration was not independently associated with mild autonomous cortisol secretion. Hair cortisol concentrations were higher in patients with mild autonomous cortisol secretion than in healthy controls, suggesting that hair cortisol concentration may capture some aspects of chronic glucocorticoid exposure in this population. However, its diagnostic performance was modest, and hair cortisol concentration was not independently associated with mild autonomous cortisol secretion after adjustment for age, sex, and body mass index. Therefore, hair cortisol concentration should be regarded as a complementary rather than a standalone biomarker, and further prospective studies are needed to clarify its clinical utility.
